extracted.intended_audience: PCT receiving Office staff and applicants/agents preparing international PCT (international application) filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Receiving Offices (and applicants/agents) on the physical and presentation requirements (Rule 11 and related provisions) for international PCT applications and related documents, and how to check and correct defects for publication, OCR and reproduction. Covers ordering/numbering of sheets, text formatting, margins, drawings/photographs, translations and procedural handling of defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with prescribed physical requirements (Rule 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must comply to the extent provided for in the Regulations with the prescribed physical requirements (Article 14(1)(a)(v)). Those physical requirements are set out in Rule 11 and relate to fitness for reproduction, size and numbering of sheets, margins, writing of text matter, drawings, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices should check compliance with Rule 11 as part of Article 14 checks. The requirements relate to reproduction fitness (scanning/OCR), sheet sizes and numbering, margins, and presentation of text and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Rules 10 and 11.1–11.13 to documents filed after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical requirements of Rules 10 and 11.1 to 11.13 also apply to any other document (for example replacement sheets, amended claims, translations) submitted after the filing of the international application (Rule 11.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-filing documents should be presented to the same physical standards as the original application; Receiving Offices must apply the same checks when such documents are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks when application filed in a language of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application is filed in a language of publication (Rule 48.3(a) and paragraph 55), the receiving Office checks whether the application complies with physical requirements to the extent that compliance therewith is necessary for the purpose of reasonably uniform international publication (Rule 26.3(a)(i)) including image scanning and optical character recognition (OCR) by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks should focus on what is necessary for uniform publication and OCR quality; strict application of every detail is unnecessary if publication/OCR will not be impaired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks of translations furnished for international search (Rule 12.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application is filed in a language of publication but a translation is furnished under Rule 12.3 for the purposes of international search, that translation is checked for compliance with the physical requirements referred to in Rule 11 only to the extent that compliance therewith is necessary for the purpose of satisfactory reproduction (Rule 26.3(a)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices check that translation sheets admit direct reproduction (photocopy/scanning) in accordance with Rule 11.2 and that the print is dark and well contrasted (Rule 11.9(d)). Since translation sheets are not used for publication, requirements are applied only as needed for reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks when application filed in non-language-of-publication and related translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application is filed in a language which is not a language of publication, the receiving Office checks the original text only to the extent necessary for satisfactory reproduction. The translation and the drawings in the language of publication are checked for compliance to the extent necessary for reasonably uniform international publication, including image scanning and OCR by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus publication/OCR checks on the translation/drawings that will be published. Original-language sheets are only checked insofar as they affect reproduction; applicant-provided translations of abstract/drawings are treated similarly under Rule 26.3 ter(a)/(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings without text need not be refiled with translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a translation is required under Rule 12.3 or 12.4 and drawings which are filed with the original of the international application do not contain text matter, such drawings need not be filed again with the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings contain no text, the same drawing sheets can be used with the translation — no duplicate drawing sheets required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Article 14 defect provisions to translated abstracts/text-in-drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant must furnish a translation of the abstract or any text matter of the drawings into a language of publication, the provisions relating to defects under Article 14, including checking of physical requirements, apply mutatis mutandis (Rule 26.3 ter(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When translations are required for publication, they are subject to the same defect-check process as original parts under Article 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct defects (Form PCT/RO/106) under Rule 26
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application does not meet the physical requirements, the receiving Office invites (Form PCT/RO/106) the applicant to correct any defect as provided for in Rule 26 (paragraphs 153 to 159).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices should use the prescribed Form PCT/RO/106 to notify applicants and allow correction where defects affect Rule 11 requirements; see Rule 26 procedures and paragraphs cited for timing and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of elements and ordering of sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the international application must be placed in the following order: the request, the description (excluding the sequence listing part of the description), the claim(s), the abstract and the drawings (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering is required for the international application to be presented correctly for processing and publication. Sequence listings are treated separately (see ST.26 entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets — separate series and drawings numbering format
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets constituting the international application must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals with the following separate series of numbering: the first applying to the request only and commencing with the first sheet of the request; the second series commencing with the first sheet of the description and continuing through the claims until the last sheet of the abstract; and if applicable, a third series applying to the sheets of the drawings only. The number of each sheet of the drawings must consist of two sets of Arabic numerals separated by a slant, the first set being the sheet number and the second set being the total number of sheets of drawings (for example, 1/3, 2/3, 3/3); see Rule 11.7 and Section 207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain three distinct numbering sequences: request, description→claims→abstract, and drawings (with 'sheet/total' format). This facilitates identification and handling of each part during processing and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning of sheet numbers (Rule 11.7(b)) — no strict objection where in margins
rubrics_metrics.description: While Rule 11.7(b) indicates that the numbers must be centered at the top or bottom of the sheet, but not placed in the margin, objections to non-compliance with this specific limitation is unnecessary where the numbers appear in the top or bottom margins but do not interfere with the areas where the receiving Office stamps the sheets with the international application number, date of receipt and any indications relating to substitute sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not object to sheet-number placement in top/bottom margins if they do not interfere with RO stamps; technical flexibility is allowed to avoid unnecessary replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing presentation requirement (ST.26 XML)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing part of the description must be presented as a separate ST.26 XML file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings are not interleaved in description sheets but provided as separate ST.26 XML per standards to facilitate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renumbering unnumbered sheets ex officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Where sheets filed on the international filing date but not numbered as part of the international application are intended to be part of the international application, the receiving Office may renumber the sheets ex officio (paragraphs 161 to 165), failing which the International Bureau will do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants fail to number sheets correctly, the RO may renumber to prevent technical defects; if not done by RO, the IB will renumber during processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing of text matter — legibility, dark indelible color and minimum character size
rubrics_metrics.description: The request, the description, the claims and the abstract shall be typed or printed in a dark indelible color (Rule 11.9). Graphic symbols, chemical and mathematical formulae and certain characters in the Chinese or Japanese languages may be hand drawn. The text must be printed in letters the capitals of which are not less than 0.28 cm high (Rule 11.9(d)) — approximately 12 point text in Times New Roman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text must be suitable for OCR and reproduction: dark ink, machine-printed where possible, and sufficiently large (≥0.28 cm capitals). Certain technical symbols and some Asian characters may be hand-drawn. Handwritten markings on request form (e.g., check-boxes) need not be objected to if legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line spacing and spacing tolerance (Rule 11.9(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 11.9(c) requires that the typing is 1½ spaced, but this need only be enforced to the extent that the lines of text are clearly separated from one another such that there is a definite vertical gap between the tops of letters and the lower part of letters on the line above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce 1.5 spacing only to the extent required for clear line separation for OCR; do not object if line separation is adequate even if not strictly 1.5 spaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance re: request form text capture and encouragement to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the request is not published as such, details such as applicant/inventor's names and addresses are captured by OCR at the International Bureau for international publication; therefore, Receiving Offices should, in their contacts with applicants, encourage them to respect similar guidelines for text matter in the request as in the description, claims and abstract, but without going as far as objecting to text matter in the request form, provided that it is sufficiently legible so as to allow correct data capture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ROs should advise applicants to format request details for OCR-friendly capture but avoid unnecessary objections to minor request-form formatting issues so long as legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margin requirements (Rule 11.6) and pragmatic flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 11.6 prescribes minimum margins for description, claims and abstract: top, bottom and right sides: 2 cm; left side: 2.5 cm. These requirements only need to be checked to the extent necessary to ensure that information is not lost in scanning and to ensure image scanning and OCR can be carried out efficiently for publication. There must be sufficient space to add necessary stamps and still have at least 0.5 cm of blank space around the edge to avoid information loss if the page is not perfectly aligned when scanned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply margins with a practical focus on preserving text for OCR and allowing space for stamps. Replacement sheets should generally be requested only for major margin defects. Letterheads or stamps with applicant/agent names and addresses may not be used on sheets. Reduced originals may be acceptable if the A4 copy meets margin and character size rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's file reference placement allowed (will be masked)
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication of the applicant's file reference, if any, on pages of the international application other than the first sheet of the request causes no problem for international publication provided that the reference is placed in the left-hand corner of the top margin, within 1.5 cm from the top of the sheet. During technical preparations, the top portion of all sheets is covered by a mask containing the pre-printed international publication and application numbers, so such a reference will be masked and will not appear in the published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-file references are permitted in the specified top-left margin location and will be masked for publication; they must not interfere with stamps/OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line numbering sequence — recommendation and when to object (Rule 11.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 11.8(a) strongly recommends that every fifth line of each sheet of the description, and of each sheet of claims be numbered, the numbers appearing in the right half of the left margin, but this is not mandatory. If lines are not numbered or numbered differently there is no basis for objection regarding reasonably uniform publication. The only reason for objection is if numbering appears somewhere other than the left margin or if there is not a clear gap between the numbering and the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line numbering is recommended for ease of reference, but ROs should not object unless numbering interferes with the main text or appears outside the left margin area without a clear gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text column and skew requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For reasonably uniform international publication and to allow image scanning and OCR, text matter in the description, claims and abstract should not be presented in more than one column. Text should not be askew (text askew by not more than 5 mm is generally acceptable since it can be corrected by the International Bureau for image scanning and OCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-column layout preferred. Minor skew (≤5 mm) acceptable; larger skew that impairs OCR may justify correction requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on drawings in description/claims/abstract and permitted content
rubrics_metrics.description: The description, claims and abstract may not contain drawings but may contain chemical or mathematical formulae and/or tables to the extent provided under Rule 11.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings are located only in the drawings part; formulae and tables are allowed in text parts as permitted by Rule 11.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and photographs standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow sheets and diagrams are considered drawings (Rule 7.1). Photographs may be filed where it is impossible to represent in a drawing what is to be shown. Where photographs are submitted, they must be presented on sheets of A4 size, respect the minimum margins applicable for drawings (top and left sides: 2.5 cm; right side: 1.5 cm; bottom: 1 cm, but with some flexibility), and be black and white; they may be submitted as originals. Regarding the standard to be applied in respect of drawings, including photographs, see Rules 11.10, 11.11 and 11.13 and the PCT Applicant's Guide, Chapter V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat photographs as drawings only when necessary and ensure they meet A4 sizing, margin and B/W requirements. Apply Rules 11.10–11.13 and consult the Applicant's Guide for drawing standards and examples.
